Theme

## Philosophy quotes about humanity

Humanity names both the species and the moral quality of being humane—bridging anthropology and ethics.

26 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

### Why this theme matters

Philosophers ask what makes humans distinctive, what we owe one another as humans, and how “humanity” can include or exclude.

### In the history of philosophy

Confucian ren, Renaissance humanism, Enlightenment rights, and critiques of humanism from various directions keep the theme contested.

### Thinkers in this collection

[Immanuel Kant](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/immanuel-kant) , [Seneca](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/seneca) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus) , [Jean-Paul Sartre](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/jean-paul-sartre) , [The Doctrine of the Mean](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/the-doctrine-of-the-mean) , [Protagoras](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/protagoras) , [Blaise Pascal](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/blaise-pascal) , [John Locke](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-locke)

### Frequently asked questions

#### What is humanity in philosophy?

It can mean the human species, shared capacities, or the virtue of humane regard for others.

#### Is human nature fixed?

Debates range from fixed essences to historical and cultural formation of human possibilities.
